subject: Publisher tenant proofing & offer gating — checklist and next steps
messages:
From: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.ai>
To: Sara Patel <sara.patel@acmeai.com>, Acme AI Marketplace Team <marketplace@acmeai.com>

Date: Wed, 21 Mar 2028 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Publisher tenant proofing & offer gating — checklist and next steps

Sara / Acme team — thanks again for the quick turnaround on the initial offer bundle. Before we move to publisher validation on the Azure side we need to align on a small set of tenant-proofing artifacts and gating decisions so the marketplace team doesn't flag the listing during verification.

High-level asks (can you confirm what you already have and what you expect Redwood to provide?):
- Tenant ownership proof: tenant ID + screenshot of subscription ownership or publisher admin.
- Service principal/managed identity details for the integration tests (app id, redirect URIs if applicable).
- Offer manifest (ARM/JSON) — we received a draft but need the SKU -> plan mapping verified.
- Co-sell enablement items: co-sell acceptance form (signed), commercial contact + PSC (partner solution contact).
- Security checklist: SOC2/ISO attestation (PDF) and data flow diagram for the offer.

I'm attaching a short runbook template for the tenant proofing artifacts (acme-offer-manifest-v1.json) and a zip template of the evidence bundle. If you can drop the missing items into our shared Drive link I will coordinate with Marissa to run the technical gate checklist.

Goal: get everything in by EOD Friday (3/24) so we can request publisher validation next week. If any of these items require legal procurement signatures, flag that now and we will route through contracts.

Thanks —
Vivek
Vivek Kulkarni

Date: Wed, 21 Mar 2028 10:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Publisher tenant proofing & offer gating — checklist and next steps

Thanks Vivek — good checklist. We have most of this but wanted to confirm a couple of implementation details before uploading:

1) Tenant proof: we can provide the subscription owner screenshot and the tenant GUID, but Acme's security team prefers to redact subscription IDs in public docs. Is the tenant GUID alone sufficient for publisher validation?

2) Service principal: we'll export the app id but will not share secrets. We will include the app manifest and the reply URLs used for the redirect flow.

3) Co-sell: sales has signed the co-sell acceptance form internally — we can upload scanned signature to the Drive. Pricing: is the SKU->plan mapping in the attached manifest enough for the marketplace team, or do you need an additional pricing CSV for the billing team?

We'll upload a preliminary evidence bundle to the Drive by EOD today. Attaching a checklist we use internally (Acme_Evidence_Checklist.pdf) for your reference.

—Sara

Head of Cloud Partnerships, Acme AI

Thanks Sara — this looks straightforward. A couple of operational clarifications from the Azure validation side:

- Tenant GUID is acceptable for the initial gating step; the marketplace team will ask for a subscription owner screenshot only if there is a mismatch. Redacted IDs are fine in the public bundle.
- For pricing, include both the SKU mapping in the manifest and a simple pricing CSV (columns: sku_id, plan_name, unit_price_usd, billing_cycle). Our billing intake system prefers CSV to speed the ingestion.
- Service principal: include app id + manifest and ensure the app has the permission set listed in appendix A of our runbook. No secrets required.

Action items I can take on from Redwood:
1) I will validate the ARM/manifest against our template and return a marked-up manifest by EOD Thursday (3/23).
2) Karthik — can you own the co-sell form intake and DocuSign link? We need the signed doc in our records before co-sell enablement.

I'll run the technical gate once the manifest + evidence bundle are uploaded. If we hit any identity proofing gaps we'll open a publisher support ticket.

Marissa
Marissa Cole
Principal, Marketplace Integrations | Redwood Inference
